description:
## Why

Incoming SMTP must deliver to the right user's mailbox. Currently stoa-smtp delivers all mail to the singleton user. With multiuser, RCPT TO address must resolve to a user_id and the message must land in that user's Inbox.

## What

- Add address → user_id routing table (or derive from the users.email column directly)
- SMTP RCPT TO handler looks up the local-part@domain against the users table
- If found: accept the message and deliver to that user's Inbox
- If not found: return 550 5.1.1 (user unknown)
- Support address aliases: an aliases table mapping alias@domain → user_id (simple many-to-one mapping; no forwarding in v1)
- Catchall address: optional config for a user_id that receives mail to any unrecognised address at the domain

## Config

```toml
[smtp]
domain = "mail.example.com"
catchall_user = "postmaster"  # optional
```

## Acceptance

- SMTP delivery to alice@domain lands in alice's Inbox
- SMTP delivery to bob@domain lands in bob's Inbox
- SMTP delivery to unknown@domain returns 550 if no catchall configured
- Aliases resolve to the correct user
- Existing SMTP auth and relay tests pass
notes: The users.email column is the primary address. The aliases table is additive. Do not implement forwarding (delivering to an external address) in v1 — that is a separate feature.
title: SMTP delivery routes to correct user mailbox by address
